condition.expression: no_confirmed_short AND vin_present AND vcc_present AND en_present AND NOT switching_measured

next_steps.action: Probe the switching node (the junction of high-side drain, low-side drain, and inductor) with an oscilloscope. Also probe the high-side and low-side gate-drive pins.

measure.what: Switching node voltage waveform + gate-drive waveforms
measure.where: Switching node = inductor input pad; gate-drive pins per controller datasheet
measure.instrument: Oscilloscope, 100 MHz bandwidth, 10x probe, ground spring
measure.expected: Square wave at the controller's switching frequency (typically 300-1500 kHz for laptop bucks), swinging between ~0 V and VIN. Gate-drive pins should show clean transitions.
measure.safety: Use a ground spring, not the long alligator clip. Beware shorting adjacent pads with the probe tip.

interpretations.then: Controller is switching. Proceed to check feedback and output voltage.

Controller is not switching despite VIN/VCC/EN all good. Likely causes: controller dead, soft-start cap shorted, fault flag latched (over-current / thermal). Check the SS/ILIM pins per datasheet before condemning the controller.

interpretations.if_result: Switching present but distorted or low amplitude
interpretations.then: Gate drive is failing or one FET is open. Check high-side and low-side gate-drive pins individually.

next_steps.requires_info_note: Need controller datasheet for switching-frequency range and gate-drive pin locations.
